_note: Generic Persian base culture (BASE_04), single-language Old Persian seeded directly from culture_axsatran.json (kept separately). The Shah/satrap court of the forested uplands and the steppe: ezafe construct-of-relation, theophoric given names on -aspa (horse) / -arta (truth) / -farnah (glory). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old-Persian/satrapal register (allowed, catalog 5.3). DEITY names are the Old-Persian-shifted morphs of the Agrippan canon (Turvasa, Urlaspa, Naumana, Arzanta, Asturna), recognizably the same powers, never real Iranian/Zoroastrian gods. The cardinal virtue is ARTA (Truth/Right-order); its opposite is DRAUGA (the Lie). The realm is religiously TOLERANT: the Shah shelters the subject cults under Asturna's peace. Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are English (or an approved foreign term - 'Shah' for the kingdom tier); the conlang forms are in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue only.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (Indo-Iranian): vowels a i u with long a/i/u; spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f; sibilants s/sh/z/zh and c(ts); r l; nasals m n; semivowels y v/w; aspirate h; characteristic endings -a, -ah, -ish, -iya, -ana, -aspa(horse), -arta(truth), -data(law-given), -farnah(glory); theophoric stems are the Old-Persian-shifted canon morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C); permitted clusters xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr-; vowel length distinctive; stress on heavy syllables; the genitive-of-relation '-ahya' (ezafe).

morphology.patronymic_form: filiation 'X-ahya puthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthra'; theophoric given names on the shifted god-stems and on Arta- (Truth); nobles a house (vith-X) or a chiliad; no inherited surname for commoners (filiation + earned epithet).
morphology.compounding_rule: quality/relation + element: Arta-xshaca (truth-realm), Vahu-farnah (good-glory), Baga-data (god-given); construct via '-ahya' (ezafe); toponyms Dida-[name] (fort of), [name]-pura (city of), Atash-[power] (fire of).

title_ladder.government: feudal - the Shah's court: the Xshayathiya (Shah) over the satraps (Xshacapavan), the chiliarch-vizier (Hazarapatish), the royal road and the king's-eye inspectors; the magi tend the fire but seldom rule.
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old Persian native register beneath English display titles, ascending. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Framatar (appointed director/governor) county over a Parada (governed district); Xshacapavan (SATRAP, protector of the realm) duchy over a satrapy (Xshacapavanam); Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a great province (Dahyu); Xshayathiya (king) kingdom - displayed as Shah, the approved foreign term; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. Rank titles are the real Old-Persian/satrapal register (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince) / Visa-puthra (the king's son)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler' - here 'Shah' at the kingdom tier). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric or Arta-/Vahu- virtue-name) + filiation (X-puthra); nobles add a house (vith-X) and a court/satrapal office; the renowned earn an honest-deed epithet.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the court-and-satrapal nobility carry a house (vith) and office; commoners use filiation + earned epithet.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names from the shifted deity-stems + an Old Persian element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X). e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah, Vahu-Arzanta.

religion._note: Deity-names are the Old-Persian-shifted morphs of the Agrippan canon (Tullaru -> Turvasa, Urlandu -> Urlaspa, Numunu -> Naumana, Argantu -> Arzanta, Rialtu -> Riyata, Itarnu -> Asturna), recognizably the same powers, never real Iranian/Zoroastrian gods. Lawful henotheist but TOLERANT: Asturna the Wise Lord most high upholds ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and the Lawful powers are His yazata-ministers; the Chaotic powers are the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie). The cardinal sin is the Lie; the Shah's word is bond. The realm shelters the cults of its subject peoples under Asturna's peace - foreign gods are tolerated in the satrapies, never suppressed.
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus / canon Itarnu; the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the king's farnah-glory, revered above His ministers)

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (the sun and Arta, lamp of right-order; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (the good mind, wisdom and the law; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Arzanta (trade, the road and increase; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy)

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Asturna the Wise Lord, Turvasa of Arta, Urlaspa of the sworn war, Naumana of the good mind, Riyata the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers the hosts of Drauga the Lie, warded; the oath and the king's word bind alike, for the cardinal sin is the Lie.
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the honest dead (the fravashi fore-spirits of the house) and the fire-altar of the hearth and the satrapy; the great powers invoked at the Atashana situationally, the king's peace kept.
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the hosts of Drauga - and names Asturna and the Lawful yazata the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers are the hosts of Drauga the Lie, each keeping its shifted name + a hostile portfolio-epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities; Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void; Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (the Lie made gold).

clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (the chief of chief magi)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana): 'the Atashana of Turvasa'; the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar) on the altar.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just kings, kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and petitioned at the fire-altar; 'the Arta-true [name]' (the righteous [name]).

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring

banks_patterns.ships: royal-road and river-barge names (a land-realm's few craft): 'Bearer of the Baji', 'the Farnah', 'Boat of Arzanta'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [number/power] Spada (host) and the Immortal-style guard: 'the Spada of Urlaspa', 'the Ten-Thousand (Anushiya)'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen apadana-halls and dead fire-temples: 'the dead Atashana of [name]', 'the buried Apadana of Dida-[name]'
